referents.why: Possessive 'your' on 'loins' in the command 'gird up your loins' is second masculine singular: the one commanded, Job.
Object 'you' of 'I will ask you' is second masculine singular: the addressee of the speech, Job.
'Make known to me': the first person inside the LORD's speech refers to its speaker, the LORD.
Implied 'you' of the imperative 'gird up' is the one the command is spoken to, Job.
First person 'I will ask': the speaker of this speech, the LORD.
Implied 'you' of the imperative 'make known' is the addressee, Job.

links.why: The waw joins a command to a yiqtol in a different person. Per the and-definition that is 'so that', not a plain and.
links.category: and after command means so that

links.why: Gird up (command) so that I will question you: the first-person yiqtol after the second-person command is its purpose.
The waw joins a command ('make known') to the first-person yiqtol before it. The asking's content is that command, so the plain and is replaced.

groups.why: The builder gave the member role 'part', which is not an imperative role. The question the command aims at is its aim.
The sender is the LORD; the builder gave a slot id (cl1s), which is not a candidate. The addressee, Job, is added.
groups.category: speaker and addressee of a question

cant_tell.what: The content of 'I will ask you' (the questions) begins in 38:4 and is not linked here
cant_tell.why: The questions are judged with their own verses; here the turn's part is only cl2.

cant_tell.what: Whether turn0 is nested in the LORD's speech turn Job.38.1#g1
cant_tell.why: The nesting is not linked from this verse; the outer turn's parts run to 38:38.

cant_tell.what: Whether 'you shall inform Me' (cl2) is the purpose of the questioning or a second demand in the same speech.
cant_tell.why: Both readings fit the waw. The purpose type is chosen because the link rule gives it for a command after a change of person; the form does not settle the sense.
